bibliographic.title: Reducing sustainable supply chain risks: a digital technology-enabled risk management framework for ESG-oriented engineering procurement
bibliographic.authors: Fenghua Cao, Lingdi Liu, Wenyan Song
bibliographic.citation_apa: Cao, F., Liu, L., & Song, W. (2025). Reducing sustainable supply chain risks: a digital technology-enabled risk management framework for ESG-oriented engineering procurement. Complex Engineering Systems, 5, 10. https://doi.org/10.20517/ces.2025.35

methodology.method_family: systematic literature review; framework development; case application validation
methodology.study_design: Systematic review of ESG and procurement risk management literature with proposed DEEP-RM framework and feasibility validation at new energy company S
methodology.sample_description: Corpus from systematic review of ESG and procurement risk management literature; single case application to new energy company S
methodology.sector: engineering procurement; sustainable supply chain; ESG-oriented procurement
methodology.technology_context: DEEP-RM framework leveraging digital technologies including Large Language Model, Multi-Agent System, Blockchain, IoT, and big data analytics for ESG-oriented circulated procurement risk management

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study addresses ESG-oriented engineering procurement risk management and positions LLM as one digital technology for document-based risk identification within a broader supply chain framework; it does not address conversational AI systems, chatbots, conversational agents, or governance of LLM-based conversational deployments in regulated environments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Python triage over-matched governance, compliance, risk, and LLM terms. The article is an Open Access Review proposing DEEP-RM for sustainable supply chain procurement risk management. LLM appears alongside Blockchain, MAS, and IoT for multi-source risk identification, assessment, human-machine solution design, and monitoring—not for conversational governance, guardrails, observability of dialogue, human oversight of conversational outputs, or regulated conversational system accountability. Conversational AI dimension scored 0/3 in deterministic triage.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, and framework description; exclusion does not hinge on ambiguous terminology.

appraisal.notes: Appraised against its own supply chain risk-management objectives. Methodological signals support a structured review plus framework proposal with case validation, but transferability to conversational LLM governance in regulated settings is low.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent supply chain risk framework with some deployment limitations acknowledged, but relevance to conversational governance of LLM systems in regulated environments is very low because LLM use is document-centric and non-conversational.

coding.theme: Digital technology-enabled supply chain risk management
coding.subtheme: LLM-assisted multi-source risk identification in ESG-oriented procurement

synthesis.main_claim: The authors propose DEEP-RM, a closed-loop framework that integrates ESG dimensions with digital technologies such as LLM, MAS, and Blockchain to improve engineering procurement risk management and supply chain resilience.
synthesis.contribution: Combines systematic review findings with a circulated procurement risk management framework and reports feasibility validation through application at new energy company S.
synthesis.limitations: Deployment barriers for SMEs include GPU costs for model fine-tuning and legacy ERP integration; the framework treats LLM generically for text comprehension and risk register compilation rather than detailing conversational system governance.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence for conversational governance in regulated LLM systems; at most peripheral contextual value for generic LLM-in-risk-management mentions.

evidence.claim: Article is a peer-reviewed journal review on supply chain procurement risk, not conversational AI governance.
evidence.excerpt: Open Access Review Reducing sustainable supply chain risks: a digital technology-enabled risk management framework for ESG-oriented engineering procurement

evidence.claim: LLM is one enabling digital technology within a procurement risk framework, not the central object of conversational governance study.
evidence.excerpt: this paper proposes a framework, namely DEEP-RM, for ESG-oriented circulated PRM that leverages DTs such as the Large Language Model, Multi-Agent System, and Blockchain

evidence.claim: Research method includes systematic review and case validation, supporting mixed methodological appraisal.
evidence.excerpt: Based on a systematic review, this study finds that current research focuses on a single Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) dimension

evidence.claim: Case application validates framework feasibility at one company.
evidence.excerpt: Meanwhile, the study's application to the new energy company S validates the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed framework.

evidence.claim: Governance references concern ESG compliance and oversight in supply chains, not conversational system governance.
evidence.excerpt: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and blockchain can support organizations in effectively managing ESG risks, improving regulatory compliance, enabling continuous oversight, and protecting privacy and security

evidence.claim: LLM role is document parsing and risk entity extraction for procurement data, not dialogue governance.
evidence.excerpt: DEEP-RM deals with PRM in four aspects: LLM-based multi-source risk identification, BDA-driven multi- criteria risk assessment, human-machine-integrated risk solutions designing, and MAS-Integrated multidimensional adaptive monitoring.

evidence.claim: LLM processes contracts, policies, and supplier documents to generate risk registers.
evidence.excerpt: Leveraging advanced text comprehension and knowledge integration capabilities, LLM can systematically process multi-source data.

evidence.claim: Authors acknowledge SME deployment constraints for LLM integration.
evidence.excerpt: Key implementation challenges include prohibitive GPU computational costs for model fine-tuning and integration complexities with legacy systems

evidence.claim: No conversational AI, chatbot, or dialogue-system governance mechanisms are described in provided text.
